title: 🔄 Passive Voice

sections.heading: When to use passive
sections.body:
Use passive voice in academic writing when:
• The doer is unknown or irrelevant
• You want to emphasise the result, not the agent
• You want a more objective, formal tone

"The data was analysed" (passive) → more academic than "We analysed the data"

sections.heading: Structure
sections.body:
Present: is/are + past participle → "Results are recorded daily"
Past: was/were + pp → "The study was conducted in 2022"
Perfect: has/have been + pp → "The policy has been implemented"
Future: will be + pp → "The findings will be published"
Modal: can/should/must be + pp → "The issue must be addressed"

highlight: In Task 1 (describing graphs), passive is very natural: "A sharp increase was recorded" or "The data shows that X was exceeded by Y."

example.wrong: We can see from the graph that researchers found interesting results.
example.right: The graph illustrates that a significant increase was recorded between 2010 and 2020.

question: Convert to passive: "Scientists discovered a new vaccine in 2023."
options: A new vaccine discovered by scientists in 2023.
A new vaccine was discovered by scientists in 2023.
A new vaccine were discovered by scientists in 2023.
A new vaccine has discovered by scientists in 2023.
correct: A new vaccine was discovered by scientists in 2023.
explanation:
Past simple passive = was/were + past participle.

✅ "A new vaccine WAS DISCOVERED by scientists in 2023"

Common errors:
❌ Missing "was": "A new vaccine discovered by..."
❌ "were" is wrong because "vaccine" is singular
❌ "has discovered" = present perfect ACTIVE, not passive

sentence: The experiment _______ under controlled conditions last year.
explanation:
"Was conducted" is correct — past simple passive for a completed action.

"Conducted" alone = active past tense (missing subject)
"Has conducted" = present perfect ACTIVE
"Is conducted" = present simple passive (wrong tense — "last year" needs past)
hint: Last year = past tense. Passive = was/were + past participle.

correct: The topic has been extensively studied.
explanation:
Present perfect passive: Subject + HAS BEEN + adverb + past participle.

Note the adverb "extensively" goes BETWEEN "been" and the past participle — a common point of error for learners.

title: Find the Passive Voice Error
instruction: One sentence uses the passive voice incorrectly:

sentences.text: The results were published in a peer-reviewed journal.
The data has been careful analysed by the research team.
sentences.explanation:
"Careful" is an adjective — it cannot modify a verb. The adverb "carefully" is needed.

✅ Correct: "The data has been carefully analysed by the research team."

In passive voice, adverbs go BETWEEN "been" and the past participle.

sentences.text: The policy will be reviewed by the committee next month.
